A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WorldMesh, with matching authors, core method, and original experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison. v3 retains Appendices A–E and adds Appendix F.

before.justification: v1 reports original generated scenes, baseline comparisons, conditioning ablations, automatic image-quality scores, and a perceptual study with 31 participants.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds quantitative 3D-consistency evaluations, component and backbone comparisons, layout-generation measurements, scaling results, and navigability analysis.

M1.justification: The scaffold construction, object reconstruction, iterative appearance synthesis, edge verification, and depth-regularized 3DGS procedure remain intact. v3 clarifies joint wall-texture accumulation and interactive segmentation, both already supported by v1 Section 3.3 and Appendix C. The alternative backbones instantiate the existing pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-guided, single-story, multi-room indoor scene generation across varied layouts, themes, and viewpoints. The separate five-scene evaluation, room-count measurements, and occupancy analysis extend assessment within this coverage; they do not establish a new domain or distinct generation task.

E2.justification: The six end-to-end baselines in Table 1 and Figure 3 are unchanged. New Table A2 adds component-level comparisons of Haiku 4.5, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B, and gpt-oss-20b against the original Opus 4.6 layout backend. Table A1 evaluates three retained scene-generation baselines on the additional evaluation set.

E3.justification: v3 adds a separate five-scene evaluation using scale-normalized cross-view depth MAE, AbsRel, and scaffold depth/normal alignment. It also introduces a 0.15 m occupancy-grid connectivity protocol, scaling measurements at 4–12 rooms, and alternative image/layout-model configurations. The original 31-participant protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 2 extends conditioning ablations with tests removing edge-recall validation, mesh-based 3DGS initialization, depth loss, and initialization plus depth loss together. Automatic ablation evaluation now spans five scenes. Appendix F additionally examines backbone dependence, layout-backend behavior, scaling cost, and free-space connectivity.

E5.justification: Table A2 newly specifies 10 runs with varying scene sizes for mean layout-correction iterations and timing. This is newly reported run information, not evidence of increased repetitions for retained experiments. Neither version supplies confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the perceptual ablation ratings are unchanged. New Table A1 reports reprojection MAE-norm of 0.1615 for NB Pro, 0.2173 for local Flux2-klein, and 0.3221 for WorldExplorer; Table 2 reports 1.8804 after removing both mesh initialization and depth loss. Appendix F adds timing, layout-generation, and 96.7% average connectivity results. Earlier single-scene automatic ablation scores are replaced by five-scene results, so their numerical differences are not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The quaternion similarity, depth-edge recall, projection expressions, and 3DGS loss remain unchanged. v3 adds empirical evaluation measures but no new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows its diagnosis of earlier approaches from lacking explicit geometry to lacking a persistent, explicit geometric representation. The principal contributions—mesh-guided multi-room synthesis, robust consistency, and linear scaling with room count—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds specific attribution of consistency gains to mesh initialization and depth loss, with smaller contributions from validation. Appendix F interprets backbone comparisons as supporting scaffold-driven gains and connectivity as supporting traversability. These refine the existing explanation; the single-story and occluded-object limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies arc-length camera spacing and 10-degree pruning, Canny thresholds of 0.1/0.3 with a 3×3 Sobel aperture, and the distilled Flux2-klein-9B configuration with four sampling steps. It also documents parallel API generation versus sequential local execution and associated timing. Interactive SAM3 annotation was already disclosed in v1 Appendix C.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Haiku 4.5, Qwen2.5-Coder, and gpt-oss, and acknowledges that recent video models incorporate camera or point-cloud geometric priors. The broader research positioning remains intact; numerous venue and bibliographic updates concern the same previously cited works.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted revisions to the wall-texturing explanation, metrics paragraph, ablation discussion, and conclusion, and adds Appendix F. Terminology, grammar, author-contact information, and cross-references are refined. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 is substantially redesigned into separate automatic and perceptual panels, while Tables A1–A3 and the occupancy visualization in Figure A5 add new displays. Figure 2 corrects its example prompt, Table 1 moves, and Figure A4 is reduced and relocated beside the study description. The original qualitative result images are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 supported its central consistency and scalability claims mainly through image-quality scores, perceptual judgments, and conditioning ablations. v3 adds direct geometric measurements across five scenes, targeted reconstruction ablations, alternative-backbone tests, and measured scaling and connectivity. Table 2 and Appendix F therefore address substantial validation gaps while retaining the original comparisons. Metric implementation details and uncertainty reporting remain limited, but the added evidence materially strengthens the paper overall.
